content.text: If you specify a particular property, you can delete it, e.g.:
DELETE WHERE { <hashuri> <
http://example.org/foo
> "bar" }
But deleting all of the userspace properties doesn't delete the resource – the server managed resources associated with it being a container stick around.
Also, trying to delete with an HTTP DELETE deletes the parent resource, e.g.:
curl -X DELETE "
http://localhost:8080/rest/foo#bar
deletes
http://localhost:8080/rest/foo,
not the hashuri.

I don't think we really know what hash-URIs mean in Fedora, anyway. They clearly aren't "anchors" in a representation. We need to get a handle on that and make sure that we aren't doing something that makes a hash of HTTP. See what I did there? Eh?
Is it possible to implement GC triggered by deleting all of the userspace properties?
Alternatively, is it possible for hash-based uri's to not be full JCR nodes, can they just be stored on the parent-URI?
It is, using JCR. As discussed on the email list, we are trying to avoid that because it severely restricts the possible future implementations of Fedora.

In the current design, if hash-URIs are going to serve as the subjects of triples, they must be associated with JCR nodes. Changing that design is certainly theoretically possible, but it would be a pretty tremendous amount of work and much
more
backward-incompatible than other suggestions that have been made to help resolve this problem. (I.e.

I think the other possibilities boil down to establishing an HTTP convention for explicitly triggering node cleanup and/or deletion.  This could be an HTTP header to indicate the hash URI fragments to delete, or a header/parameter/etc. to trigger the deletion of all hash URI fragments with no properties or referents, etc.
So, not just associated with, but strongly associated with?  So that the node representing
http://example.org/fedora/rest/node1
could not own the triples with the uri
http://example.org/fedora/rest/node1#sub1

Justin-- any subject must have its own node. Period. One-to-one. As I said, that could be changed, but if you have problems with back-incompatibility from FCREPO-1801, you will be much less happy with this idea.
Esmé-- -1 in a big way to inventing magic Fedora-specific headers (or even worse, params) for this kind of subject selection. That sounds more-or-less like we're breaking HTTP at that point.

So, I don't know much about the Fedora implementation, so please help me understand.  The impression that I get is that Fedora has tightly coupled resources (the graph I get when I fetch a URI) with the data layer (what triples that live on that graph mean).

The benefits of tight coupling, is that you can check referential integrity.  And you don't have to figure out if a DELETE or UPDATE means update just the graph I'm pointing at or all the triples with this as my subject.
The drawback being that hash URIs don't really have a place in the scheme.

So one solution (which is probably hard to implement) would be to decouple the resources from the data they represent. Then impose constraints which ensure that you can't add/update triples on a resource they shouldn't go on.  That is, you can add
http://example.com/fedora/rest/123#sub1
on
http://example.com/fedora/rest/123
but not on
http://example.com/fedora/rest/321
.  Would something like this be theoretically possible?  Or do I have I misconceived the whole idea?
I don't really understand what you mean by "decouple the resources from the data they represent". Are you talking about some kind of abstraction layer?

I suppose you could call it an abstraction layer.  I guess what I'm saying is add a type of node called "graph" which has a URI. The Graph object could contains 1-n child nodes that represent objects.  The objects would be identified by a unique subject URI (and the relationship to the parent graph).  Typically the child node shares the URI of the graph uri, but it may also be a sub-uri like a hash code or a b-node.
When you make a HTTP request it should return/update all the nodes in the Graph corresponding to the URI. Referential intergrity / GC is applied only to the child nodes.
Fedora could apply constraints on the children ensuring you don't put an object into a graph where it doesn't belong (non-matching URIs).
This could decouple the resource layer (graph) from the data layer.
Justin, that's pretty much exactly what we have now. It clearly does not solve the problem of nodes elsewhere in the repository making links into hash-URI nodes.
I guess I don't understand what the problem is with nodes making links into the hash-URI nodes then. Can you explain it to me?
It's explained very well in

's first comment on this very ticket. If you allow that (as we currently do), then you cannot discover when to delete the hash-URI node without using JCR's special ability to know when links are pointing back into it.

So to reiterate: The problem is that I want to be able to delete the hash resource via a sparql query on the parent, which is equated to "magically delete the JCR resource when it doesn't have any triples left in it", but we don't want triples on outside objects to disappear if we do that?
Why the assumption that I don't want those outside triples to disappear when I delete all the triples from a hash URI?

Because we have to make the assumption one way or another, and we sure as heck don't want to make it to the side of "Assume that the user just doesn't care and delete anything we need to delete to get this request finished."
Alright. It would have been nice for my use cases if that happened, but I can see why we'd want to go the careful route.
"Fedora: Careful to a fault, so you don't have to be."

The current behavior: if all the user-managed triples about a hash URI fragment are removed, then the node remains in place, but is invisible.  This could result in very large numbers of empty hash URI fragments hanging around.
Here's a PR that remove them:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/982

Given our other choices (not including server-managed triples, not providing an explicit deletion mechanism), I think removing them when there are no user-managed/visible properties associated with them.
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/a71298f4817887538112dccc1979ad40956c8ff3
When you create a fragment URI, I would expect to be able to delete it by running sparql update on the parent resource and doing something like
DELETE
{ <hashuri> ?p ?v }
WHERE {
<hashuri> ?p ?v .
but doing so throws errors that it can't delete the server managed triples on that resource.
